Seminar Title:

Development of Sustainable Recycling Techniques for Fiber-Reinforced Epoxy Composites and Their Reuse

Seminar Type:

Speaker Name:

Abstract:

The surge in glass/epoxy composite waste generation underscores the urgent need for a sustainable recycling technique. This research focuses on addressing the challenges of chemical recycling, including solvent and polymer reusability, the complexity resulting from the use of solvent combinations, and the environmental effects of chemicals. The developed thermo-chemical recycling technique utilizes a single synthesis grade Dimethyl Sulfoxide (DMSO) to reclaim intact recycled glass fabrics (RGFs) from waste glass/epoxy laminates. The glass/epoxy laminates were immersed in DMSO solvent and subjected to different temperatures (130℃, 150℃, and 170℃) for different time durations (45, 60, and 90min) inside a hot-air oven for glass fabrics recovery. Recycling glass/epoxy at 150℃ for 60min consumed only 25mL and yielded better quality fabrics. The FTIR analysis of residual DMSO confirmed that there were no significant changes in the IR spectra of residual DMSO solvents when compared to pure DMSO solvent, indicating the reusability of the DMSO solvent. Leveraging the reusability of residual DMSO, another glass/epoxy wastes were recycled at 150℃ to recover glass fabrics. Similarly, the IR spectra of residual epoxy that got suspended in residual DMSO solvent resembled that of epoxy, indicating its reusability as a filler. Further, the flexural strength of RGF150/epoxy (fabricated using RGFs from recycling at 150℃ and pristine epoxy) was determined to be ~6% lower than virgin glass fiber reinforced epoxy composites (VGFECs). However, the strain at peak for RGF150/epoxy was marginally higher than VGFECs. The inter-laminar shear strength of RGF150/epoxy was significantly higher by ~26% than VGFEC.
